newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Mexico markets seen weathering U.S. vote.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mexico markets seen weathering U.S. vote.

text.p: The attack by the U.S. Congress on Mexico's anti-drug efforts will rattle nerves in that country's already skittish financial markets, but it is unlikely to cause any breakdown, analysts said on Thursday.

Earlier, the U.S. House of Representatives approved a bill to overturn the Clinton administration's certification of Mexico as a full ally of the United States in the war against illicit drugs. The vote was seen as a symbolic referendum by U.S. lawmakers on corruption in Mexico's government.
To ease the blow, the House suspended sanctions usually required by so-called decertification and gave Mexico a 90-day grace period to show progress in its anti-drug efforts.
Also, it appeared the House could not muster enough votes to overcome a likely veto of the bill by Clinton.

"It doesn't change the fundamental economic story in Mexico and is really only a blip on the long-term radar screen, but it can create short-term problems because of a lack of confidence in Mexico," said James Carlen, head of emerging market analysis at American Express Financial Services.
